newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Scotts sinks into red due to provisions.
newsitem.headline: Scotts sinks into red due to provisions.

text.p: Retail and property group Scotts Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it incurred losses in 1996 due to provisions made for amounts owing by directors' related companies and losses from its overseas associates.
In a note accompanying its results for the year ended June 30 1996, Scotts reported a pretax loss of Singapore $8.8 million against a profit of S$11.7 million in the previous year.
Scotts said the loss was due to provisions made to directors' related companies of S$3.2 million.
Its various overseas associated companies also incurred losses amounting to S$4 million for the group.
The group also said it had yet to receive certain payments, which were due June 15 1996, from its Indian property investments from businessman Raj Kumar Jatia.

Scotts said to comply with Indian regulations, it has become necessary for the group to restructure its investments in India. Accordingly a provision of S$1.2 million has been made to write down its investment to net realisable value.
On the current year's prospects, Scotts said it expects to report improved results for the group.
It said it will launch its property projects in Singapore and Malaysia soon and profit will be recognised gradually.
Its service apartments in London is also expected to report improved results.
